questions.q: What is the key difference between OUTER APPLY and CROSS APPLY?
options: OUTER APPLY keeps every left-side row even when the function returns nothing; CROSS APPLY drops it
OUTER APPLY can only be used with system functions
CROSS APPLY is faster but functionally identical
There is no difference — they are interchangeable
questions.explain: This is the entire point of OUTER APPLY — it's the LEFT JOIN-style equivalent of CROSS APPLY.

questions.q: Which regular JOIN type does OUTER APPLY behave like?
options: LEFT JOIN
INNER JOIN
RIGHT JOIN
CROSS JOIN
questions.explain: OUTER APPLY : LEFT JOIN :: CROSS APPLY : INNER JOIN — the exact same match/no-match behavior, applied to a function instead of a table.

questions.q: What appears in the function's output columns when OUTER APPLY finds no rows for a given input?
options: NULL, for every column the function would have returned
An empty string
The row is silently dropped instead
The query throws an error
questions.explain: Same NULL-filling behavior as LEFT JOIN's unmatched right-side columns.

questions.q: When would you specifically want OUTER APPLY instead of CROSS APPLY?
options: When you need every calling row to appear in the report, even if the function's lookup came back empty for some of them
Only when working with numeric functions
Never — CROSS APPLY should always be preferred
Only inside a stored procedure
questions.explain: If dropping unmatched rows would hide people/records that should still show up in a report, OUTER APPLY is the right choice.

questions.q: How is the CROSS APPLY / OUTER APPLY relationship best described?
options: The identical concept as INNER JOIN vs. LEFT JOIN, just applied to a function instead of a table
Completely unrelated concepts that happen to share similar names
OUTER APPLY replaced CROSS APPLY in modern SQL Server versions
CROSS APPLY is used for text data; OUTER APPLY for numeric data
questions.explain: If you understand INNER vs. LEFT JOIN, you already understand CROSS vs. OUTER APPLY — same logic, different right-hand-side source.
